title: Evidence for evolution
group: BIO-EVOL / BIO-ECOL / BIO-PLANT — Evolution, Ecology & Plants
examples: What is the difference between homologous and analogous structures?
How do fossils help us understand past life?

explain.say: Today we will look at evidence that supports evolution.
Fossils are preserved remains of ancient life forms.
A fossil record shows life changing over deep time.
Homologous structures show shared ancestry in different species.
DNA evidence shows shared genetic code among all life.
When we look at the structure of the bacterial flagellum, it resembles components of an eon. This suggests common ancestry.

faq.q: What is the difference between homologous and analogous structures?
faq.a: Homologous structures share a basic underlying bone pattern because they came from a common ancestor. For example, the bones in a human arm and a bat's wing are homologous.

faq.q: How do fossils help us understand past life?
faq.a: Fossils provide physical evidence of organisms that lived and died millions of years ago. They show us how life forms have changed over geological time.
asks: Can we see dinosaurs in fossils?
What kind of evidence do fossils give?

faq.a: Yes, comparing DNA sequences reveals similarities that match evolutionary predictions. The more closely related two species are, the more similar their DNA will be.

faq.q: Are all similarities due to evolution?
faq.a: No, some similarities can happen by chance or due to similar environmental pressures, but the pattern across multiple lines of evidence points to evolution.
A transitional fossil shows intermediate traits between an ancestral group and its modern descendant group. For example, Archaeopteryx shows links between reptiles and birds.

facts: Fossils are preserved remains of ancient life in rock layers.
Homologous structures have similar underlying bone arrangements.
DNA sequences contain genetic information inherited from ancestors.
The fossil record shows gradual changes in life forms over time.

quiz.say: Which type of evidence shows underlying structural similarities across different species?
quiz.why: Homologous structures, like the bones in a human arm and a whale flipper, share a common bone pattern indicating shared ancestry.

wrong.0: These structures look similar but evolved independently, like a bird's wing and an insect's wing.
wrong.1: The fossil record shows what life was, not the underlying structure of living organisms.
wrong.2: While DNA is evidence, the specific structural comparison is best represented by homologous bones.

quiz.say: What evidence shows a sequence of life forms over vast periods of time?
quiz.why: The fossil record provides a timeline showing the sequence of life forms that existed in the past.

wrong.1: These structures compare living organisms, not the sequence of life over millions of years.
wrong.2: DNA shows relatedness in living species, but the fossil record shows the actual physical sequence.
wrong.3: These are remnants in modern bodies, not a record of entire past life forms.

quiz.say: If two species have very similar DNA base pairings, what does this suggest about their relationship?

options.show: They share a recent common ancestor
options.say: They share a recent common ancestor

quiz.why: High similarity in DNA sequences strongly suggests that the species inherited their genetic material from a relatively recent shared ancestor.

wrong.1: Small differences in DNA are expected even between closely related species.
wrong.2: High similarity points toward shared origin, not separate origins.
wrong.3: DNA comparison is one of the most direct and powerful pieces of evidence for common descent.
